checks.what: russian-empire loss to polish-lithuanian-commonwealth, Sep 1772, of Vitebsk+Mogilev oblasts minus Cliopatria's Russian 1772 shape (132 cells, 33,400 km2, 26.3-29.8 E). Page: Russia took 'the commonwealth territories east of the line formed roughly by the Dvina, Drut, and Dnieper rivers' (counties of Vitebsk, Polotsk, Mstislavl and Inflanty); 'ratified by its signatories on September 22, 1772'. Dossier ledger/21 (1772-09 gain) names all of Vitebsk and Mogilev, so the western remainder (Braslaw-Lepel-Bobruisk side) was the dossier's overreach. Trial vs a no-patch baseline: the 132 cells stay Polish 1772-1779 (baseline: unowned 1772-1774). Side effect: Poland's 1775 keyframe now differs by under 20 cells and no longer snaps, so 2 cells it used to restore (26.51 E 55.69 N near Braslaw; 27.73 E 48.41 N in Podolia), released in 1772 by the 1772 keyframes, stay unowned 1775-1779.

spanish-louisiana loss to nobody, Jan 1770, of Minnesota minus the west-of-river polygon (432 cells). Page: 'Upper French Louisiana was split with Britain at the Mississippi River, with the west going to Spain'; Spanish Louisiana 'encompassed the entire Mississippi Basin to the west, starting from the right bank of the Mississippi River'. The polygon's river line (Winona, Red Wing, St Paul, Elk River, St Cloud, Little Falls, Brainerd, Aitkin, Grand Rapids) is right at cell scale. Its north edge is the 47th parallel, so everything north of 47 N counts as east bank. In the trial, spanish-louisiana held only 21 cells there (4 west of Grand Rapids, the Mississippi headwaters); the rest was already Rupert's Land through the p1760-p1769 rulings. Effect: 94 east-bank cells plus 21 northern cells go unowned 1770-1773, the same as the rest of the Indian Reserve (Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio are unowned 1770-1773 in the trial). Quebec takes 86+25 of them in 1774. 8 east-bank cells near St Cloud and Little Falls lie between the river and Quebec's own polygon: unowned 1774, Spanish Empire 1775-1779 (baseline: spanish-louisiana); the window agent already flagged them.

thirteen-colonies gain from british-colonial-empire, Jan 1770, of Maine (299 cells). Page: the charter 'took effect on May 14, 1692, and included the Massachusetts Bay Colony, the Plymouth Colony, the Province of Maine, the Territory of Sagadahock...'; 'Maine was not separated until after American independence, when it attained statehood in 1820' (the quote is verbatim). The dossier's 1763 and 1768 keyframes say 'without Maine, then part of Massachusetts', which is self-contradictory: Maine belonged to a member colony. Trial: Maine is thirteen-colonies 1770-1775 (baseline: the umbrella 1770-1774 and unowned in 1775), then 215 cells go to the USA in 1776 by its own keyframe; northern Maine (84 cells) stays unowned from 1776, as before.

viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata_1776: the original correction (first union member, unchanged) plus Puno (263 cells) and the Jesuit Missions region within Brazil (235 cells, 53.5-56.4 W, 27.5-29.5 S, the Misiones Orientales). RdlP page: 'Governorate of Chucuito (1776-1784)', 'Political and Military Government of the Misiones Guaranies (1776-1810)', 'Intendancy of Puno (1784-1796)', Puno 'became part of the Viceroyalty of Peru in 1796'; the Misiones Orientales, 'part of the Political and Military Government of the Misiones Guaranies', were captured in 1801-1802. The RdlP page names only Chucuito for 1776-1784, so I checked the whole of Puno on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intendancy_of_Puno: in 1776 Carabaya, Lampa, Azangaro and Paucarcolla plus the government of Chucuito 'became part of the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata', which covers all five partidos, i.e. modern Puno. Trial: Puno is RdlP 1776-1779 (baseline: unowned 1776, Spanish Empire 1777-1779) and the Misiones are RdlP 1776-1779 (baseline: Spanish Empire), which gives the dossier's own 1796 and 1801 losses land to remove. Side effects: 10 edge cells of the Jesuit Missions spec (around 53.5 W and 27.5 S) pass from colonial-brazil/portuguese-empire to RdlP in 1776. Portugal's 1778 keyframe now differs by no more than 20 cells and no longer snaps, so 16 cells in the upper Rio Negro, Roraima and Amapa (64 W 1-4 N, 61-63 W 3.6-4.5 N, 52.3 W 3.2 N) stay unowned 1778-1779 instead of Portuguese, and 2+2 cells there swap Spanish/Portuguese.

spanish-empire_1772: the override's first operand is byte-for-byte the dossier's correction, minus Minnesota east of the river (the same polygon as events/1). It is supported by the same page sentences as events/1. No other window overrides this shape. Trial: the umbrella no longer takes the 94 east-bank and 24 northern Minnesota cells in 1772-1773 (3 northern cells it held go unowned), and nothing else changes. The Spanish Empire keyframes of 1775-1778 still include the gazetteer's Louisiana region and keep the 8 east-bank cells (flagged by the agent).

spanish-louisiana over province-of-quebec 1774-1779 in Minnesota west of the river (412 cells). Province of Quebec page: the Act ran 'west to the Mississippi River'; Louisiana (New Spain): 'starting from the right bank'. Trial: it settles 87 cell-years (1774), and all 412 cells stay spanish-louisiana 1774-1779 (baseline: Quebec took 87 in 1774). The why's figures (87 of 194) match the published conflict.

province-of-quebec over british-colonial-empire 1775-1779, no region. Page: the province 'was established by the Kingdom of Great Britain in 1763'; the Act extended it 'from the coast of Labrador on the Atlantic Ocean' and west to the Mississippi. Trial: it settles 1,166 cell-years (453 in 1775, 243 in 1776, 470 in 1778). By admin-1, every ruled cell is Quebec Act land: Quebec 346-351, southern Ontario 7-55, the Labrador coast 30-45 (all at 52-58 N on the mainland, none on Newfoundland island), and Michigan, Illinois, Indiana and Minnesota 1-11 each. No cell of Maine, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, New York or Vermont is involved. The St Lawrence region (1,648 cells) is Quebec throughout 1774-1779; in the baseline 346 went to the umbrella in 1775 and 178 were unowned in 1776-1777.

rupert-s-land over province-of-quebec 1774-1779, no region. The page supports the quote: the Act extended the colony 'to the southern boundary of lands owned by the Hudson's Bay Company, or Rupert's Land'. The ruling settles 468 cell-years in 1774, all cells Rupert's Land held before 1774. But the why described them wrongly as '266 cells of north-western Minnesota'. In fact 202 are in northern Minnesota at 47-49 N and 91-96 W (the rupert-s-land dossier's 47-49 N box, not only the north-west), and 266 are in the 49-50 N band of north-western Ontario.
checks.fix: Corrected the why's cell figures and places, and marked the change as a reviewer edit. The entry's logic is unchanged. Re-ran --check-patch: 8 ok.

patch_check: --check-patch p1770-p1779: 8 entries, 8 ok, 0 rejected (after the reviewer's why-text fix to rulings/2). Trial: all 8 applied; rulings settle 87, 1,166 and 468 cell-years.
problems: rulings/2 rests on the rupert-s-land_1670 Minnesota polygon, a box from 47.0 to 49.0 N and 90.5 to 97.3 W. Its southern strip at 47-47.7 N (roughly 90 of the 202 cells) is Lake Superior north-shore and St Louis River drainage and the Mississippi headwaters, not Hudson Bay drainage. The ruling hands it to Rupert's Land for 1774-1779, and the p1760-p1769 rulings do the same for 1762-1769. The 49-50 N Ontario band also takes in part of the Lake Nipigon (Great Lakes) basin. This is a dossier-level fix: move the polygon's south edge to the Laurentian divide, from a page that gives it.

Keyframe-snap threshold side effects of this patch (trial against a no-patch baseline), all small. Poland's 1775 keyframe no longer snaps, leaving 2 cells unowned 1775-1779 (near Braslaw and in Podolia). Portugal's 1778 keyframe no longer snaps, leaving 16 cells unowned 1778-1779 in the upper Rio Negro, Roraima and Amapa instead of Portuguese.

8 Minnesota east-bank cells near St Cloud and Little Falls lie between the river and the Quebec 1774 polygon (whose line runs from 93.2 W 45.0 N to 95.2 W 47.2 N). They are unowned in 1774 and Spanish Empire 1775-1779, both Spanish-coloured as before. The window agent flagged this. Fixing it needs the Quebec polygon to follow the river, or the gazetteer 'Louisiana' region to stop at the river.

The window agent's boundary notes stand: the p1780-p1789 window should extend the Quebec-over-umbrella and Quebec-boundary rulings to the Quebec 1774 keyframe's end (1782). The p1790-p1799 and p1800-p1809 windows should check the RdlP 1796 (Puno) and 1801 (Misiones) losses, which now have land to remove.
